To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the odds of a patient having a positive response to treatment are higher when a clinician considers the patient’s biomarkers and that the odds of having a negative response are higher when a patient’s biomarkers are not taken into account.

(1) the odds for a treatment response or intolerance to a given medication can be predicted by a person’s genetic makeup; (2) the odds are not 100% certain, but they are better than chance; (3) the odds are best for the most common genetic variants, which are found in 50% to 80% of individuals; and (4) the odds are better when the genetic information is used in conjunction with other patient-specific information.
“the best treatment for a specific patient is the one that has the highest odds of success and the lowest odds of adverse effects, based on that patient’s specific biomarkers.”
